subject.title: Generalize post-timeout compaction completion reconciliation across session state

question: Should OpenClaw promote the existing count-only late-success repair into an authoritative compaction-completion reconciliation boundary, and which session fields should that boundary own before implementation?
rationale: The source gap is real, but deciding whether the boundary owns only durable accounting or also status snapshots, outcome metadata, auth-profile rotation, memory flush state, and recovery events is an architecture/product choice.

options.title: Design the boundary first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design item and ask session-state owners to define field ownership plus monotonic/idempotent semantics before implementation.

options.title: Limit to narrow bugs
options.body: Keep the count-only repair and handle each stale status/activity field through focused follow-up issues or PRs without a shared completion event.

options.title: Declare current behavior sufficient
options.body: Close the broad follow-up if maintainers intentionally want only the count reconciliation and no shared compaction completion boundary.

recommendation.title: Design the boundary first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design item and ask session-state owners to define field ownership plus monotonic/idempotent semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest recent history on the merged compaction reconciliation precursor and the session write seams likely to host this boundary.
